claims.text: GUARD: the run reported on EXACTLY the frozen nodes, or say what moved.
claims.why: The code computes declared and observed sets and returns error strings if extra or missing nodes exist.

claims.text: A runner is injectable, and a gate is a subprocess whose output is parsed; either could in principle report a node that is not in the frozen set (a parser that matched too loosely, a runner that expanded a selector).
claims.why: No code in this chunk defines or references a runner, gate, or parser; claims about their behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: A result computed over a set that is not the declared one is not the measurement that was declared, so it is refused rather than reported.
claims.why: The function returns error strings when extra or missing nodes are detected, thus refusing the result.

claims.text: verified is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed.
claims.why: The field verified is set based on logic in judge_before_state; the docstring description matches the code's behavior (verified=True only if no bad_f2p and no bad_p2p).

claims.text: Anything else is either an invalid task or an unobtainable verdict, and reasons says which.
claims.why: judge_before_state sets invalid=True or unrunnable=True with reasons accordingly.

claims.text: Pure: turn before-state node statuses into a verdict about the TASK.
claims.why: The function takes inputs and returns a BeforeState without side effects (pure).

claims.text: Three separate refusals, in this order: 1. NO VERDICT (not_run) -> unrunnable. 2. A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> invalid. 3. A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> invalid.
claims.why: The code checks unknown first (unrunnable), then bad_f2p (invalid), then bad_p2p (invalid), matching the order and logic.

claims.text: An unknown never becomes a fact in either direction.
claims.why: When unknown nodes exist, the function returns BeforeState with unrunnable=True and does not proceed to check other conditions.

claims.text: Passing refutes the claim outright; skipped is not evidence of failure; missing means the node id does not exist even with the test overlay applied, so the task names a test that is not there.
claims.why: The code generates specific reason strings for PASSED, MISSING, and other statuses, and marks invalid=True.

claims.text: A regression set that is already red proves nothing about a patch, because every candidate 'passes' it by not making it worse and 'fails' it for reasons that predate the change. Noise wearing a number is worse than no number.
claims.why: The code marks bad_p2p as invalid and provides a reason explaining that a regression set that is already red cannot detect a regression.

claims.text: The declaration, written into the receipt so a reader can check that what was measured is what was declared -- and so the gate can refuse a task whose lists moved after it was verified.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows a receipt or gate logic; the claim references external usage.

observations.what: guard_measurement_match function is defined but not shown with 'def' in this chunk; it appears as a standalone docstring and body without a function signature.
judge_before_state sets duration_s on the returned BeforeState even when returning early due to unknown or bad nodes.
The docstring for BeforeState says 'reasons says which' but the field is named 'reasons' (plural) and is a tuple of strings.
to_dict includes 'selection_digest' from self.selection.digest, but the dataclass field is 'selection' (not 'digest'). The code assumes selection has a 'digest' attribute.
